rect(AB, CB) = sq(AC) — area equality from 2.11 construction

configuration_map: Three collinear points A-C-B on a single line segment. Point C is constructed by Proposition 2.11 as an interior point of segment AB such that the rectangle contained by AB and CB equals the square on AC. No triangles, circles, or off-line points are involved. The entire configuration is one-dimensional.
pass_reason: The proof's spatial content is minimal — a single collinear point C between A and B on a line segment. All subsequent reasoning (proportion from 6.17 converse, magnitude comparison from 5.14) is algebraic/proportional and fully consistent with C lying between A and B. No angle decompositions, no inside/outside claims, no ray orderings. No pair of spatial claims contradicts any other.
